speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe exactly where you feel your weakness in the upper limbs, and do you experience any drooping of the eyelids or slurred speech along with your double vision?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The pattern of symptoms—double vision worsening with specific eye movements and proximal muscle weakness that fluctuates with activity and improves with rest—is classic for Myasthenia Gravis. I would like to confirm this with a Tensilon (edrophonium) test or Acetylcholine Receptor Antibody levels.
